title: Africa capitals two of six · The Sahel and the Gulf of Guinea
edition: Africa capitals · Six regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the Africa capitals, episode two of six. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Now the western coast, where the Sahel meets the Gulf of Guinea and the Atlantic trade has left its marks.

states.name: Dakar
lines: Dakar stands on the Cap-Vert peninsula, the westernmost point of the African mainland, on the Atlantic.
The city grew from a harbour on that peninsula, and nearby Gorée Island carries a memorial house that remembers the island’s role in the Atlantic slave trade.
Remember the peninsula city at the far west, with Gorée in the bay and the mainland running east.

states.name: Banjul
lines: Banjul stands on an island in the mouth of the River Gambia, on the Atlantic coast of The Gambia.
The country takes its name from the river that reaches the sea here; the British founded the capital in 1816 as Bathurst, and it took the name Banjul in 1973.
Remember the capital on an island in the river mouth, one of the smallest capitals in Africa, inside the narrow country inside Senegal.

states.name: Bissau
lines: Bissau lies on the Rio Geba, on the small Atlantic coast of Guinea-Bissau, south of Senegal.
The Bijagós archipelago lies just offshore, an island world of mangrove channels and sea-turtle nesting beaches.
Remember the turtle islands off the small coast below Senegal; Guinea-Bissau and Guinea are two different countries.

states.name: Conakry
lines: Conakry stands on the Kaloum peninsula, on the Atlantic coast of Guinea, at the mouth of the Niger River.
Its name comes from the Susu word for “beyond the waters”, describing the crossing from the islands at the river mouth; the city began on the island of Tombo.
Remember “beyond the waters” on the Kaloum peninsula, with more than 3,500 mm of rain a year, one of the wettest capitals in the world.

states.name: Freetown
lines: Freetown stands where the Sierra Leone River meets the Atlantic, on the coast of Sierra Leone.
It was founded in the 1790s for people freed from slavery, and the great cotton tree where the first freed settlers are said to have given thanks in 1792 stood until a storm brought it down in 2023.
Remember the freed-people settlement at the river mouth, in the small country between Guinea and Liberia.

states.name: Monrovia
lines: Monrovia stands on a cape on the Atlantic coast of Liberia, the country between Sierra Leone and Côte d’Ivoire.
It was founded in 1822 by American colonists and named after President James Monroe; the iron pier it exported from still stands in the harbour.
Remember the American colony capital on its cape, with the iron pier in the harbour.

states.name: Yamoussoukro
lines: Yamoussoukro stands inland in the forested heart of Côte d’Ivoire, north of the coast where Abidjan carries the country’s trade.
It became the national capital in 1983, and its Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, modelled on St Peter’s in Rome, is among the largest churches in the world.
Remember the inland capital with the huge basilica, well north of the lagoon coast.

states.name: Accra
lines: Accra stands on the Gulf of Guinea, on the coast of Ghana between Côte d’Ivoire and small Togo.
Kwame Nkrumah declared Ghana’s independence here in 1957, and three European forts — Dutch, Danish and British — still stand on the old shoreline.
Remember the fort coast capital, where independence was declared and where Nkrumah’s mausoleum now stands above the square.

states.name: Lomé
lines: Lomé stands on the Gulf of Guinea, behind a narrow strip of beach, in the southern part of Togo.
Its Grand Marché was ruled by the “Nana Benz”, women cloth traders rich enough to be driven in Mercedes cars.
Remember the cloth-trading queens of the Grand Marché, on the beachfront capital at the Ghana border.

recap: Dakar stands on the far western peninsula, Banjul on an island in the river mouth, and Bissau below Senegal on the turtle islands.

Remember “beyond the waters” at Conakry, the freed-people settlement at Freetown, the American cape at Monrovia, the inland basilica at Yamoussoukro, the fort coast at Accra and the beachfront arch at Lomé.
